correctness.rationale: The real periodic gradient g=f′ has |g|≤1 and mean zero; convolution commutes with gradient, making the exact dual quotient norm min_c∫|k_t−c|. Jacobi triple product proves ordinary heat is strictly geodesically decreasing on (0,π), and positive α-stable subordination preserves this for α<1. Its unique median level is k_t(π/2) and equality in L∞/L1 duality forces signed semicircle gradient, integrated to a triangular wave. Integrating Fourier modes on a semicircle yields the odd alternating series. Roncal–Stinga torus jump kernel and off-neighborhood small-time Lévy limit yield κ_α=(2c_α/α)(2/π)^(2α)β(2α)>0; α=1 periodized Gaussian tail and Mills asymptotic give 8√t/(π√π)e^(−π²/(16t)). Fresh independent Poisson α=1/2 arctangent comparisons and slope κ=2/π agree to high precision; limit statements remain analytical.

value.rationale: Sharp smoothing on a natural compact group is a central analytic benchmark. The quantitative discontinuity between jump-driven linear loss and Gaussian exponentially small loss, together with a fixed equality class, is mathematically motivated and useful in exact semigroup estimates, not merely restating contractivity.

final_claim: For real Lipschitz functions modulo constants on the 2π-circle and 0<α≤1, exact semigroup Lip→Lip norm is (4/π)Σ_{j≥0}(-1)^j exp[-t(2j+1)^(2α)]/(2j+1), with one triangular-wave extremizer family at all α,t>0; short-time loss is linear with explicit positive Dirichlet-beta coefficient for α<1 and Gaussian superalgebraic e^(−π²/(16t)) at α=1.
limitations: Only real geodesic circle, isotropic fractional generator and fixed 0<α≤1; not uniform as α approaches endpoints.
Rigidity at t>0 only; at t=0 all Lipschitz functions trivially attain the identity norm.
residual_risks: The α=1 endpoint and α=1/2 special case are known and cannot count independently as new.
Hidden optimal-transport interpretations may imply all α profile if they explicitly supply strict radial median and stable-subordinator kernel; no claim of universal priority.
